TTFT ~94 ms, 257 tok/s, gross CV 1.4%, powermetrics observed at ~8.8-8.9 Hz; short prefill energy is below the current detection capability and is not a quantitative result (D-055).</td> <td><code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-06-slice-2i-first-real-energy.md</code></td> </tr> <tr> <td>2026-07-06</td> <td>third update / powermetrics telemetry</td> <td>The powermetrics telemetry adapter and privileged sampling path were brought up, preserving raw plists and exposing the real sampling-rate constraints.</td> <td><code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-06-slice-2h-powermetrics.md</code></td> </tr> <tr> <td>2026-07-06</td> <td>third update / pre-hardware hardening</td> <td>Slice 2N closed the evidence-path hardening before real hardware: raw evidence retention, measured-window markers, rail validation, shared bundle reading, and post-hoc reduction.</td> <td><code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-06-slice-2n-pre-hardware-hardening.md</code></td> </tr> <tr> <td>2026-06-12</td> <td>first/second updates / mock vertical slice</td> <td>The mock-first harness reached an end-to-end auditable run path before hardware time: typed config to complete bundle, validation, reduction, and report.</td> <td><code>docs/run_reports/2026-06-12-phase-2-mock-vertical-slice.md</code></td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p><strong><a href="project_status_full.html">Full project status →</a></strong></p> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>PROJECT_STATUS.md · commit 1af9f92 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

JouleWise</title> <script>document.documentElement.classList.add("js-enabled");</script> <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css"> <link rel="icon" href="data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 100 100'><text y='.9em' font-size='90'>⚡</text></svg>"> </head> <body> <header class="site"> <nav class="nav"> <a class="brand" href="index.html"><span class="dot"></span>JOULEWISE</a> <div class="links"> <a href="index.html">Project</a> <a href="research.html">Learn</a> <a href="advisor_brief.html">Advisor Brief</a> <a href="project_status.html">Status</a> <a href="status.html">Live Status</a> <a href="roadmap.html">Roadmap</a> <a href="process.html">Process</a> <a href="record.html">Record</a> <a href="library.html" class="active">Sources</a> <a href="results.html">Measurements</a> </div> </nav> </header> <main> <div class="doc-layout"> <aside class="toc-sidebar"><div class="card-label">Table of contents</div><a href="#current-state">Current State</a> <a href="#verify">Verify</a> <a href="#release">Release</a> <a href="#run-the-harness-mock-target-no-hardware-or-extras-needed">Run The Harness (mock target — no hardware or extras needed)</a> <a href="#config-and-schema-verbs">Config And Schema Verbs</a> <a href="#documentation-map">Documentation Map</a></aside> <div class="doc-wrap doc-source-readme-md"> <p class="doc-meta"><a href="library.html">Back to sources</a> · rendered from <code>README.md</code></p> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="README.md · commit 1af9f92"><span class="source-file">README.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 1af9f92</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise</h1> <p>JouleWise is an extensible measurement harness for energy-wise LLM inference across heterogeneous local hardware. The benchmark layered on that harness is the frozen workload suite, run rules, and strict validator. The name is a deliberate nod to JouleSort and Splitwise: energy measurement as the spine, split inference as the first major research application.</p> <p>The harness is designed around three stable ideas:</p> <ul> <li>Typed experiment configs define what should run.</li> <li>Runtime and telemetry adapters define how each hardware target is exercised and measured.</li> <li>Run bundles preserve raw traces, events, metadata, logs, and summary metrics for later audit and analysis.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Status:</strong> research prototype. The Mac (Apple M3 Max) measurement harness has completed its instrument repair (D-078 phase 0) and the repaired path has collected 229 strict members across four bracketed windows, a5-a8. Those windows are non-claim-bearing diagnostic, instrument-proving evidence, not published floors. The SCREEN+BUDGET rules are ratified and merged (D-078 clause 10; council C-033): they screen gross and idle-subtracted energy separately, retain a nonzero drift allowance for each family, require a fresh 24-hour bound, reject fallback-clock members from floor cells, and bar mock evidence from claims. The next step is one clean prospective quiet-machine window following <code>docs/phase_2/window_runbook.md</code>, producing the first claim-grade floors before the a8 re-verdict and Splitwise sizing.</p> <p>The post-audit architectural verdicts remain deliberately bounded: AXI-SB is <code>supported</code> for native static-batch runtime feasibility with request-scoped observability, while AXI-SC is <code>unsupported_for_joulewise</code> on the pinned runtime because the required speculative-decode/MTP observability or execution surface is absent. Neither is energy evidence. This summary does not select work: the generated state-kernel regions in <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> and <code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code> own live gates and next-task state. Quiet-machine execution still requires the lead-controlled hardware lane with Ed. The verified end-user quickstart remains a Phase 5 deliverable.</p> <h2 id="current-state">Current State</h2> <p>Phase 1 is in its final stretch; <strong>Phase 2&#39;s Mac vertical slice is complete and the project has its first real energy measurements</strong> (2026-07-06). From a typed config, one command produces a complete, schema-valid, auditable run bundle and reduces it to energy/latency summary metrics — proven first on deterministic mock adapters, and now live on real hardware: the MLX runtime + <code>powermetrics</code> telemetry adapters measured Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (4-bit) on an Apple M3 Max. <strong>P2-003, gross energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~47.2 J per 512-token request. <strong>P2-003, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~44.4 J per request and ~79-90 mJ per generated output token (mean 86.8 mJ). Throughput was 257 tok/s. These are legacy L1 preliminary observations (pre-2M, manual review) under <code>docs/contracts/claims_ladder.md</code>; metric bases per <code>docs/contracts/token_normalization.md</code>. The six real corpus bundles pass <code>validate-bundle --strict</code> read-only and unrewritten: strict re-derives the recorded powermetrics power trace from raw plist evidence, re-derives summary metrics from the recorded trace and event log, checks the legacy additive summary comparison, and requires shape-valid provenance for new-era bundles. This validates the recorded evidence path; it does not independently rerun the hardware session.</p> <p>Unless a figure explicitly states otherwise, JouleWise uses gross measured energy within the named measurement boundary as the headline basis. Gross energy retains the idle, model-residency, and runtime overhead present during the measured interval, so comparisons across devices, configurations, and split versus monolithic execution use gross energy. Idle-subtracted energy is reported separately as a within-device secondary view of activity above the measured idle baseline; it is not used to rank devices or configurations. In Q4, the fixed term is estimated from the gross-energy workload sweep and is not set equal to measured idle energy. The advisor-review rationale and full basis/boundary rule are recorded in <a href="PROJECT_STATUS.md#measurement-methodology-highlights"><code>PROJECT_STATUS.md</code></a>.</p> <p>Under D-070, static batching, speculative decoding / native MTP, MoE versus dense execution, quantization, and reasoning-length variance are five stress tests of Q4&#39;s single thesis. The harness must instrument all five axes and all five have strict-valid L0 smoke-bundle support plus characterization commitments, but every study remains floor-gated, capped at L2, and sequenced after Window A. See the fuller <a href="PROJECT_STATUS.md#summary">Q4 architectural stress-test agenda</a> in <code>PROJECT_STATUS.md</code>.</p> <p>D-075 now folds a ranked extension-axis evaluation into that same agenda without proliferating theses: DSpark/DFlash break-even and control riders, on-device quantized KV, one named hybrid pair, and attached cache/context/kernel/backend provenance work. Every admitted unit remains a floor-gated candidate at or below L2 with a named forbidden upgrade; unresolved runtime and device-fit questions stay NEEDS-WEB, and Ed retains commitment authority. Separate lead-run DSpark/DFlash smokes established native MLX execution and per-round observability only. Their thinking-mode, unmatched-output throughput inversion is hypothesis-generating, not energy evidence.</p> <p>Window A remains open and still requires Ed and a quiet Mac. The repaired instrument has produced the 229-member a5-a8 diagnostic collection, and the merged screening and uncertainty-budget rules (D-078 clause 10) are ready for prospective use. The next claim attempt must follow the run-book: mint the drift bound inside the quiet window, then collect a start triplet, midpoint reference, and end triplet around the science members. A passing window will support the first claim-grade floors; only then do the a8 re-verdict and Splitwise sizing follow. The earlier 222-bundle floor publication remains a caveated historical record. Use the generated state kernel—not this summary—to select the next live or agent-lane step.</p> <p>A separate nine-bundle follow-on is now available as an explicitly <strong>exploratory, unmatched, no-claim</strong> observation block. All nine bundles are strict-valid and collection-usable but claim-evidence-flagged; each model ran three repetitions of the fixed five-item sentinel shape and emitted 1,280 generated output tokens per bundle.</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>unmatched configuration</th> <th align="right">mean gross suite energy — Apple M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails (CPU + GPU + ANE)</th> <th align="right">mean gross energy/generated output token — same boundary</th> <th align="right">runtime-observed output throughput</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>OLMoE-1B-7B BF16</td> <td align="right">229.028 J</td> <td align="right">178.928 mJ/token</td> <td align="right">122.361 tok/s</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Qwen3-4B INT4</td> <td align="right">362.772 J</td> <td align="right">283.416 mJ/token</td> <td align="right">106.519 tok/s</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Qwen3.5-122B-A10B INT4</td> <td align="right">1072.273 J</td> <td align="right">837.713 mJ/token</td> <td align="right">39.473 tok/s</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>These points differ in model scale, architecture, tokenizer, and quantization, so they do not establish a controlled scaling relation, architecture effect, or efficiency comparison. The stored per-generated-token field is idle-subtracted and appears only as D-067&#39;s labeled within-device secondary view in the <a href="docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-exploratory-block/results.md">bundle-cited extraction</a>, which also records spreads, every repetition, the floor comparison, and the Qwen thinking/config caveats.</p> <p>Remaining backends plug into the same adapter interfaces: the fixture-first 2K NVIDIA stack (SSH transport, node worker, nvidia-smi + vLLM adapters) includes NV-GATE-2 software hardening: per-backend raw-lineage verifier registration, usage-first vLLM streaming, and identity-aware process-survival handling. The NV-5 localhost lead gate passed 3/3, but ALL remote protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL pending first live hardware contact; Jetson Orin (2L) remains gated on device access.</p> <p>The landed C-028 arc includes the frozen analysis manifest, the production-uncertainty path, the campaign-verdict split, idle-dependence/HAC uncertainty, the inter-token metric, doctor preflight, and the contrast/claim engine. The analysis trio—manifest, verdict split, and contrast/claim engine—is complete. The six frozen legacy arms and 0.3.x/0.4.x dispatch rules remain explicit; landed software is not being presented as new live evidence. P0-003 closed with an iCloud Drive backup and a fresh restore that was strict-valid and byte-identical. No new live NVIDIA or quiet-Mac measurement is claimed here.</p> <p>The post-audit landings add request-scoped AXI-SA burst/decode semantics, freeze SPLIT-AP Part I before outcomes, close SITE-02&#39;s discovery and emitted-code regression work, and establish AXI-SB&#39;s <code>supported</code> verdict from lead-run B=2/B=4 Metal probes. The probes establish runtime feasibility and request observability only; they add no energy result. The corresponding AXI-SC pinned-runtime spike returned <code>unsupported_for_joulewise</code>: the external- draft path lacks the full proposal/acceptance/decode-boundary observability contract, and native MTP lacks a usable generation surface. No Mac energy leg was minted from that negative applicability result.</p> <p>The repository currently contains:</p> <ul> <li>Typed config and output schemas with JSON-Schema export and validation.</li> <li>Runtime, telemetry, and transport interface contracts, with shipped mock adapters and a backend registry.</li> <li>The runnable harness: bundle writer, controller lifecycle, reducer, a shared bundle read layer, static HTML report generator, and a CLI (<code>run</code>, <code>validate-bundle</code>, <code>reduce</code>, <code>report</code>).</li> <li>Example Mac-local and mock-local configs.</li> <li>Phase 1 methodology, feasibility, and measurement-design docs.</li> <li>A test suite run in CI on every push, including a mock end-to-end run and bundle validation. The canonical command below and CI output own the current result; reader docs intentionally do not copy its volatile count.</li> </ul> <h2 id="verify">Verify</h2> <pre><code class="language-bash">python3 -m unittest discover -s tests

<h1>JouleWise: Project Status, Plan, And Architecture</h1> <p>Audience: project advisor. This is the standalone monitoring document - it summarizes what the project is, how it is built, where it stands, and what it needs, without requiring any other file. Pointers into the repository are provided for anyone who wants the full evidence trail.</p> <ul> <li>Freshness owner: phase completion lives in the phase exit checklists; live gates and work selection live only in the generated state-kernel regions of <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> and <code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code>; the canonical suite command and CI own the current verification result. This page deliberately does not duplicate volatile commit, pull-request, queue, or test-count facts.</li> <li>Repository state: <code>main</code> contains the repaired measurement instrument (D-078 phase 0) and the audited screening and uncertainty-budget rules (D-078 clause 10; council C-033). The repaired-instrument collection has 229 members across four bracketed windows, a5-a8. Those windows are useful diagnostic evidence that the instrument works, but they are not claim-bearing and do not yet publish a floor. The next step is one clean prospective quiet-machine collection following <code>docs/phase_2/window_runbook.md</code>; if it passes, it will produce the first claim-grade floors before the a8 re-verdict and Splitwise sizing.</li> <li>Project phase: see the phase exit checklists for exact completion state; live eligibility and next work come from the generated state kernel, not this reader-facing summary.</li> <li>Repository: <code>github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</code> (branch <code>main</code>)</li> <li>Live status site: <a href="https://quiet-signal-6af8833395.lakebed.app">https://quiet-signal-6af8833395.lakebed.app</a> (Lakebed capsule; it is an Ed-deployed snapshot, not the repository authority. <code>docs/site/DRIFT.md</code> records known differences; agents refresh that report when front-facing state changes and never regenerate or deploy the site.)</li> </ul> <h2 id="current-repository-view-30-second-read">Current Repository View — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>The repaired instrument has completed its first collection era, but the first claim-grade floor is still ahead.</strong> The D-078 phase-0 repair fixed the timing and calibration path on 2026-07-22. Four bracketed windows then collected 229 strict members (a5-a8). They are retained as non-claim-bearing diagnostic, instrument-proving evidence: they showed that the repaired path works and exposed the remaining drift-screen problem, but they are not a published floor set.</p> <p>That problem is now resolved in the merged SCREEN+BUDGET rules (D-078 clause 10). Gross and idle-subtracted energy are screened separately; each passing window keeps a nonzero drift allowance in its uncertainty budget; the drift bound expires after 24 hours; fallback-clock members cannot support a floor; and mock evidence is identified from the bound configuration and barred from claims. The next quiet session will mint its bound inside the window and collect three start references, one midpoint reference, and three end references. The older 222-bundle floor table below remains visible as a caveated historical record, not the current measurement posture.</p> <p>AXI-SB remains <code>supported</code> for native static-batch runtime feasibility with request-scoped observability; AXI-SC is <code>unsupported_for_joulewise</code> on the pinned runtime because the required speculative-decode/MTP observability or execution surface is absent. Neither verdict is an energy result. Remote protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL, and the generated state kernel remains the work-selection authority.</p> <h3>Published Window-A floor summary</h3> <blockquote> <p><strong>CAVEAT (2026-07-19 soundness audit):</strong> a trace-time-anchor defect was found in the powermetrics evidence path (power timestamps misaligned with runtime events at the ~0.5–1 s scale). It affects the corpora behind this table; every row below is <strong>under re-adjudication</strong> and none should be cited as a promoted floor until the instrument is repaired and the rows re-extracted. Record: <code>docs/reviews/2026-07-19-measurement-soundness-audit.md</code>.</p> </blockquote> <p>Every energy value below is a false-effect guard floor in joules on the <strong>Apple M3 Max / powermetrics SoC-rail boundary (CPU + GPU + ANE)</strong>. Gross is the D-067 headline basis; idle-subtracted values are labeled within-device secondary views. Absolute rows use repeated identical conditions; comparative rows use same-condition ABBA blocks. Each primary row uses <code>n=10</code> strict-valid bundles or ABBA blocks.</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>window / basis</th> <th align="right">absolute floor</th> <th align="right">comparative floor</th> <th align="right">computed <code>floor_gate_j</code> / disposition</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>mid request, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.527 J</td> <td align="right">0.909 J</td> <td align="right">0.909 J</td> </tr> <tr> <td>mid request, idle-subtracted — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.537 J</td> <td align="right">0.894 J</td> <td align="right">0.894 J; within-device secondary</td> </tr> <tr> <td>short request, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.052 J</td> <td align="right">—</td> <td align="right">absolute floor only</td> </tr> <tr> <td>short request, idle-subtracted — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.059 J</td> <td align="right">—</td> <td align="right">absolute floor only; within-device secondary</td> </tr> <tr> <td>prefill phase, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">1.477 J</td> <td align="right">1.739 J</td> <td align="right">1.739 J</td> </tr> <tr> <td>decode phase, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.786 J</td> <td align="right">1.027 J</td> <td align="right">1.027 J</td> </tr> <tr> <td>short-prefill stress, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.027 J</td> <td align="right">—</td> <td align="right">smoke-only; <code>not_resolvable_sample_count</code></td> </tr> <tr> <td>suite item, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">0.333 J</td> <td align="right">4.923 J</td> <td align="right">4.923 J; drift review required</td> </tr> <tr> <td>suite level, gross — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails</td> <td align="right">1.664 J</td> <td align="right">24.619 J</td> <td align="right">24.619 J; drift review required</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>The start/end NEG-8 reference pair is an <code>n=2</code> drift diagnostic, not a campaign floor. Its gross request energy moved by 7.659 J; the idle-subtracted within-device secondary view moved by 6.608 J (same boundary). Verified extraction: <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-floor-extraction/extraction-verified.json</code>; reader deliverable: <code>docs/advisor_briefs/2026-07-17-window-a-brief.html</code>.</p> <h3>2026-07-19 re-calibration under the environment guard — PRELIMINARY</h3> <p>The caveated suite rows were re-measured in two bracketed windows under the D-077 guard: <strong>94 strict-valid bundles</strong>, all admission predicates satisfied. Reviewed readout: suite gross <strong>147.96 ± 0.39 J</strong> clean (contaminated cells were ~+30%); frozen-estimator provisional comparative floor <strong>≈ 1.13 J (~0.77%)</strong> from 5 of 10 planned ABBA blocks (~22× tighter, same estimator, than the caveated figure); long-decode <strong>83.9 mJ/output-token</strong>, matching the 07-17 decode cell to ~0.1%. That corpus was claim-ineligible on source provenance (dirty collection tree); details: <code>docs/advisor_briefs/2026-07-19-recalibration-update.html</code>.</p> <p>UPDATE (2026-07-19 night): the clean re-run is done — 288 strict-valid bundles with clean source provenance (<code>runs_recal3/4/5/6_20260719/</code>) cover every planned Window-A cell except DF-TELEM at planned n, including the complete n=10 suite-ABBA comparative cell; the source provenance gate is closed. <strong>SUPERSEDING UPDATE (2026-07-19/20): a same-day soundness audit found a timing bug, and no energy number from the existing recordings will be used for claims until re-measurement.</strong> In plain terms: the power meter and the workload log time on two different clocks, and our alignment between them could be off by up to ~1 second. Energy is computed by summing meter samples inside the workload&#39;s start/stop window, so a misaligned window integrates the wrong slice of the recording — dramatic for sub-second test runs (one 0.37 s run read 0.27 J when its true consumption, plainly present in the recording, was <del>8 J), and a meaningful hidden uncertainty (</del>±10 J) even on 60-second runs. Nothing measured negative; the recordings are intact and self-consistent; long-run repeatability (~0.3% across nights) shows the platform is stable. Very short workloads are simply below this instrument&#39;s resolution and will not be claimed — by design, not workaround. The fix (align on the meter&#39;s own timestamps, attach an explicit uncertainty range to every number, calibrate end-to-end with 40 precisely-timed GPU bursts before new data) is implemented and in adversarial review. Plain-language explainer: <code>docs/advisor_briefs/2026-07-20-timing-defect-explainer.md</code>; technical record: <code>docs/reviews/2026-07-19-measurement-soundness-audit.md</code>.</p> <p><strong>REPAIR COMPLETE (2026-07-22): the instrument repair is finished and signed off.</strong> Over three days the timing defect was fixed and the whole measurement chain was hardened through nine rounds of independent adversarial review (each round tried to break the instrument; the last round found one remaining gap, recorded below). In plain terms, the instrument now: (a) knows precisely when its power readings happened relative to the model&#39;s work (the clock-alignment fix, with the alignment uncertainty — about 27 milliseconds — carried into every result as an explicit error bar); (b) proves its own calibration is genuine and fresh — a calibration recording that was tampered with, mislabeled, taken under the wrong procedure, or older than 24 hours is automatically rejected; and (c) refuses to report a result rather than report a doubtful one, in every failure case we could construct. One known limitation is recorded honestly: the file that stores the detection-floor statistics is not yet cryptographically tied back to the raw measurements it came from, so we only trust such files when our own pipeline produced them in the same verified session (a fix is queued). Live validation on the real hardware passed: the validation recording (made under the earlier 40-pulse calibration procedure) detected all 40 calibration pulses with no false detections, and a test measurement reproduced the expected physics where the old defective pipeline had been wrong by a factor of ~28. Production measurements will use the newer 59-pulse calibration procedure, which supports the stronger statistical guarantee we quote for the timing error bar. Next: a fresh calibration and re-collection of the measurement campaign under the repaired instrument. Record: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-20-p0-instrument-repair.md</code>.</p> <p><strong>COLLECTION ERA UPDATE (2026-07-24): the repaired instrument has now been proven in production.</strong> Over two nights we collected 229 clean measurements across four properly-bracketed windows. The standout result: two identical reference measurements taken three hours apart agreed to within 0.007 joules on a ~38.5 joule task — about 0.02%, which is excellent repeatability for whole-system power measurement. The windows are not yet &quot;claim-grade&quot; for one honest reason: our own stability check (comparing a reference task at each window&#39;s start and end) was found to be asking a mathematically unanswerable question, so it failed every window on a technicality while the underlying data was good. After a formal debate between the two AI models working on the project — which the reviewing model won on one substantive point — the check was redesigned and ratified: windows are now screened for anomalous drift against a limit derived from measured repeatability (instead of an arbitrary constant), and any drift observed is carried into the results&#39; error bars rather than being ignored once a window &quot;passes&quot;. Reference measurements are also being tripled at each window edge. One collection session under the new rules produces the project&#39;s first claim-grade detection-floor table, which then sizes the Splitwise replication experiments. Records: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-23-window-a-collection-arc.md</code>, decision log D-078 clauses 8-10.</p> <p><strong>SCREENING RULES BUILT, AUDITED, AND MERGED (2026-07-25; council C-033).</strong> The redesigned stability screen described above is now implemented and on main: both energy families are screened separately, every passing window carries an explicit drift allowance into its error bars, drift limits expire after 24 hours so stale calibrations cannot be reused, and a measurement whose internal clock had to be guessed can never anchor a result (that one rule alone corrected a floor that was overstated by roughly a factor of three). The code went through an unusually deep adversarial review — four independent audit rounds and three rounds of cross-examination between two different AI models — which caught and fixed several ways the new rules could have been silently bypassed. The step-by-step measurement procedure for the next collection session is written up in <code>docs/phase_2/window_runbook.md</code>. Records: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-24-screen-budget-gauntlet.md</code>, council log C-033.</p> <h3>Exploratory follow-on — not a promoted claim</h3> <p>Nine additional strict-valid, collection-usable bundles cover three repetitions each of unmatched OLMoE-1B-7B BF16, Qwen3-4B INT4, and Qwen3.5-122B-A10B INT4 configurations on the fixed five-item <code>jw_mixed_v1_sentinel</code> shape. Every bundle is claim-evidence-flagged, the model/config points differ in architecture, scale, tokenizer, and quantization, and the repetition count is below the headline protocol. The values are therefore descriptive <strong>EXPLORATORY / L1-legacy observations only</strong>.</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>unmatched configuration</th> <th align="right">mean gross suite energy — Apple M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails (CPU + GPU + ANE)</th> <th align="right">mean gross energy/generated output token — same boundary</th> <th align="right">runtime-observed output throughput</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>OLMoE-1B-7B BF16</td> <td align="right">229.028 J (227.141–231.790 J)</td> <td align="right">178.928 mJ/token (177.454–181.086 mJ/token)</td> <td align="right">122.361 tok/s (122.261–122.481 tok/s)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Qwen3-4B INT4</td> <td align="right">362.772 J (362.642–362.903 J)</td> <td align="right">283.416 mJ/token (283.314–283.518 mJ/token)</td> <td align="right">106.519 tok/s (106.470–106.545 tok/s)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Qwen3.5-122B-A10B INT4</td> <td align="right">1072.273 J (1061.722–1085.144 J)</td> <td align="right">837.713 mJ/token (829.471–847.769 mJ/token)</td> <td align="right">39.473 tok/s (39.349–39.569 tok/s)</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Each bundle emitted 1,280 generated output tokens. Gross per-output-token values above are derived from the gross suite numerator; the stored <code>energy_output_token_j</code> field instead uses the idle-subtracted numerator and is retained as a labeled within-device secondary view in the full extraction. For the like-for-like suite-level gross window on the Apple M3 Max / powermetrics SoC-rail boundary, the exploratory OLMoE-versus-Qwen3-4B mean gap is 133.720 J, above the published 24.619 J suite-level gross <code>floor_gate_j</code>. That only says the descriptive gap exceeds the measurement guard: unmatched configurations, evidence flags, drift review, and the lack of a prospective contrast still prohibit efficiency or architecture claims. Every aggregate and raw repetition is bundle-cited in <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-exploratory-block/results.md</code>.</p> <h2 id="previous-update-as-of-2026-07-09-c-027-whole-project-council-review-30-second-read">Previous Update (as of 2026-07-09, C-027 whole-project council review) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>The project put itself in front of a hostile examiner and corrected its own front page.</strong> A seven-lens cross-model review (new Codex model, extra-high reasoning) plus an independent final examiner audited the docs, the scientific claims, the statistics implementation, the architecture, and the operating loop itself. Verdict: the evidence discipline and instrument core are sound, but reader-facing claims had drifted from the evidence (the 1.5B per-token headline used the wrong denominator — now corrected as <strong>P2-003, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~79-90 mJ per generated output token), the D-053 contrast-CI machinery exists as binding specs but not yet as code (now owned as queue rows P2-037..P2-042 and gating Window-A interpretation), and the loop&#39;s own audit trail and the capstone-critical path (grading rubric, report skeleton, off-machine backup, one data-to-figure slice) need attention before any new breadth. All measured values above remain legacy L1 preliminary observations. Full adjudicated record: <code>docs/reviews/2026-07-09-c027-whole-project-review.md</code>.</p> <h2 id="previous-update-as-of-2026-07-09-advisor-status-cockpit-30-second-read">Previous Update (as of 2026-07-09, advisor status cockpit) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>The public preview is being upgraded for live advisor observation.</strong> The project-status page remains generated from repository evidence, but Lakebed now has a narrow fail-soft live overlay contract: freshness from GitHub commit checks plus parsed current fields from <code>PROJECT_STATUS.md</code>, <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>, <code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code>, and the risk register. The advisor cockpit adds live snapshot state, attention items, campaign readiness, evidence cards, and claim-ceiling panels; the Story page drops hand-authored volatile counts. The operational policy is D-051: repo markdown remains the source of truth and Lakebed never hides static provenance. Current work follows <code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code>: C-019 shakedown, then P2-015 quiet calibration for Window A (the CP-5 stop card was cleared 2026-07-09).</p> <h2 id="previous-update-as-of-2026-07-08-all-four-streams-merged-30-second-read">Previous Update (as of 2026-07-08, all four streams merged) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>Everything landed.</strong> The multi-stream session merged as four PRs: P2-013 and P2-014 are closed — all 31 audit pins fixed, the suite passed with zero expected failures (current count authority is RUN_STATE.md Current Verification; the suite-build merge was 732 tests and the post-alignment state is 734), bundle provenance now records prompt/workload identities, and <code>validate-bundle --strict</code> includes the powermetrics raw-plist-to-trace gate plus the legacy additive-summary comparison. The six existing real corpus bundles pass strict read-only and unrewritten; strict proves re-derivation of the recorded evidence, not independent rerunning of the hardware session. New-era bundles must carry shape-valid provenance to pass. The Stage 3.0.1 KV spike is merged with a lead-reverified verdict of <code>replay_supported</code> (tokens identical; cache size +0.018% vs prediction) — Phase 3&#39;s central technical risk is retired on current hardware. The fixture-first 2K NVIDIA stack is merged; ALL its protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL until first live hardware contact (the live-verification checklist is ready). The independent project critique now carries a second-pass reassessment (its recommendations that became code are marked resolved; 16/17 of its checkable claims were lead-verified against file evidence): <code>docs/project_critique_review.html</code>. Next: the detection-floor calibration (P2-015) then the 2M two-model baseline campaign on a quiet machine. Reader-facing status below defers to the phase checklist matrix rows for per-item authority.</p> <h2 id="previous-update-2026-07-07-fifth-update-30-second-read">Previous Update (2026-07-07, fifth update) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>The instrument grew four capabilities in one session and is now campaign-ready.</strong> <em>(Historical claim; C-027 (2026-07-09) supersedes the gating: execution is conditioned on P0-003 backup, P2-038, P2-039, and P2-015-SMOKE.)</em> Five parallel work streams landed (PRs #2-#6): (1) <strong>statistical uncertainty</strong> — every multi-repetition experiment now carries per-metric 95% confidence intervals with outlier detection and explicit below-protocol flags, re-derivable byte-identically from the raw evidence bundles (verified on a live 3-repetition run as <strong>D-014 verification workload, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> 99.19 ± 1.36 mJ/output-token); (2) <strong>contamination detection</strong> — an idle-window quality gate that mechanically flags runs taken on a non-quiet machine (it caught its first real contamination during verification); (3) <strong>deep telemetry</strong> — per-sample GPU/CPU-cluster frequency and residency forensics plus a machine-state snapshot in every bundle; (4) <strong>campaign automation</strong> — a deterministic config-matrix generator and a resumable sequential runner, so the planned two-model baseline matrix (4 workload shapes × 2 models × 5 repetitions) runs unattended. A review council also produced a hardware-tiered research agenda: 16 questions answerable on current hardware alone, 10 more behind planned gates (<code>docs/research_question_bank.md</code>). The P2-013 evidence-integrity and P2-014 provenance fixes are now complete; next Mac corpus step is the baseline matrix on a quiet machine.</p> <h2 id="previous-update-2026-07-07-fourth-update-30-second-read">Previous Update (2026-07-07, fourth update) — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>A flagship-class model is now benchmarked.</strong> Qwen3.5-122B (Feb 2026 generation, 122B-parameter mixture-of-experts with 10B active, a reasoning model) ran through the identical harness and workload on the M3 Max. <strong>FLAGSHIP-001, gross energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~304.0 J per 512-token request. <strong>FLAGSHIP-001, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~298.7 J per request and ~583 mJ per generated output token. Throughput was 46 tokens/s, and the gross-energy sample CV was 0.3% across three sequential repetitions in one warm-cache session. The earlier model recorded <strong>P2-003, gross energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~47.2 J per request and <strong>P2-003, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~87 mJ per generated output token at 257 tok/s. <em>(Metric bases and CV wording corrected 2026-07-09, C-027.)</em> First cross-model finding: the two measured points differ in size, architecture, and quantization, so they are not a demonstrated scaling law. They are, however, consistent with the fixed-vs-marginal structure Q4 models: <strong>unsubtracted decode-window mean power — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~23.5 W for P2-003 and ~27.5 W for FLAGSHIP-001, while the bigger model&#39;s cost showed up mostly as time. Also this update: the research agenda grew to six named questions (Q4-Q6) after a multi-model review council, with a curated question bank (<code>docs/research_question_bank.md</code>) and an instrument roadmap (richer telemetry parsing, a difficulty-graded scored workload suite, and implementing the statistical-uncertainty protocol) queued.</p> <h2 id="update-ledger">Update Ledger</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>date</th> <th>label</th> <th>one-line outcome</th> <th>run-report link</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>2026-07-19</td> <td>Measurement-soundness audit (Ed-directed)</td> <td>VERDICT: unsound for claim-bearing use as recorded — trace-time-anchor defect misattributes request/phase energies (all four P0s lead-verified); metric-level prechecks already failed 238/288 request metrics; four cooldown cap hits unjoined; analysis-engine wire incompat. Corpora demoted to instrument evidence; published 07-17 floor table caveated; instrument-repair path defined.</td> <td><code>docs/reviews/2026-07-19-measurement-soundness-audit.md</code></td> </tr> <tr> <td>2026-07-19</td> <td>Extended clean-provenance re-collection</td> <td>266/266 strict-valid bundles with clean SOURCE provenance from clean main (288 total with the completion window); all planned cells except DF-TELEM executed at planned n; one unlock abort quarantined (guard&#39;s 4th live catch); Sol recompute audit PASS on arithmetic. See the superseding soundness-audit row above for claim status.</td> <td><code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-19-recal456-extended-window.md</code></td> </tr> <tr> <td>2026-07-19</td> <td>Suite re-calibration under the guard (preliminary, review-corrected)</td> <td>94 strict-valid bundles; suite 147.96 ± 0.39 J clean; provisional comparative floor ≈ 1.13 J (~0.77%, 5/10 blocks); claim-ineligible on provenance pending clean re-run; three-lens review corrected two over-promoted claims.</td> <td><code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-19-d077-recal-window.md</code></td> </tr> <tr> <td>2026-07-18</td> <td>Contamination diagnosis + environment-guard hardening (D-077)</td> <td>Suite-cell inflation attributed to the macOS video screensaver on an awake idle display (43/50 bundles; power-source hypothesis refuted); suite comparative cells caveated pending re-run; the D-077 guard (preflight, idle admission, cooldown v2, claim barrier, anchor custody) was built and taken through an eight-round adversarial arc.</td> <td><code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-17-environment-guard.md</code>; <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-18-d077-fix-rounds.md</code></td> </tr> <tr> <td>2026-07-17</td> <td>exploratory block + D-075 re-wrap</td> <td>Nine retained OLMoE/Qwen bundles re-validated and extracted as unmatched, claim-evidence-flagged exploratory observations; DSpark/DFlash smokes and D-075&#39;s ranked extension-axis intake folded in without promoting evidence; Ed&#39;s manual site deployment recorded as the new drift baseline.</td> <td><code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-17-window-a-floors.md</code> (final re-wrap addendum; lead gate pending)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>2026-07-17</td> <td>Window A floors + advisor brief</td> <td>PRs #72/#74 closed the bounded powermetrics drain defects and P2-038 passed on merged main; PR #73 filed the AXI-SC negative verdict; 222 strict-valid floor bundles extracted and independently verified, claim-readiness caveats retained; advisor brief shipped.</td> <td><code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-17-window-a-floors.md</code> (LEAD-ACCEPTED)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>2026-07-16</td> <td>audit close + no-hardware resumption batch</td> <td>PR #66 closed the comprehensive audit; docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-param-scaling-energy.md:4514:docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-extension-axes/axes-evaluations.json:4:  "summary": "This axis is the mirror image of the DSpark/DFlash case: the science is real but the runtime-observable surface that made AXI-SA cheap does not exist here on the primary instrument. Speculation earned first-class counters because MLX-native ports (e.g. ARahim3/mlx-dspark, per the web memo) emit per-round proposed/accepted signals; nothing in the repo, the vendored clone (zero sparsity mentions), or the memo grounds ANY Apple-Silicon runtime that actually skips FFN compute from activation sparsity — a ReLU-fied checkpoint on MLX runs dense, so on the Mac the axis is energy-invisible by construction (that null is itself a reportable row). The exercisable leg, if any, is the 3080 Ti: the PowerInfer lineage targets consumer NVIDIA GPUs with ReLU-fied checkpoints, but current 30-series/12 GiB support and artifact availability are NEEDS-WEB, and Deja Vu's artifact is A100-class research code (NEEDS-WEB). On reduction: the whole-request contrast reduces cleanly to existing patterns — C5-1.8's stack-conditioned runtime attribution (sparse runtime vs dense runtime differ in more than sparsity) and C5-1.12's model-surgery divergence discipline (ReLU-fied model is not the base model); what is genuinely new is only the dynamic-active-parameter question — whether energy tracks a per-request activated-parameter fraction, turning C5-1.1's static active-parameter coefficient input-dependent under the Q4 thesis — and that question is gated on a runtime counter no fleet runtime is grounded to expose. Identifiability is therefore the binding constraint: sparsity leaves token streams untouched (same tokens, same counts, no decode_emission analogue), so the harness sees only the whole-request energy shadow unless a self-reported, harness-unverifiable runtime counter appears. Process note: a Sol high read-only scout was launched via the audited codex-run-v3 path per the skill, but the workflow deadline landed before its envelope returned; per protocol a missing envelope is never treated as a result, so this evaluation is lead-grounded in the named repo files and the web memo, with all ungrounded runtime claims marked NEEDS-WEB. Net: a thin 3080 Ti-leg contrast and one likely-null Mac row are cheap and honest; a first-class sparsity axis is not currently buildable to AXI-SA standard.",

docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-param-scaling-energy.md:5241:docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-floor-extraction/extraction-verified.json:65:        "notes": "DERIVATION (docs/phase_2/detection_floor.md §Estimator rule, lines 91-97). Absolute cells: r_i = E_i - mean(E) over strict-valid bundles; floor_abs_j = max(max_i|r_i|, t_{0.975,df=9} * s_r * sqrt(1 + 1/10)) with t_{0.975,9} = 2.2621571628 (table value; scipy unavailable), sqrt(1.1) = 1.0488...; spread_j reported is s_r (sample stddev of residuals = sample stddev of E). Comparative (ABBA) cells: delta_i = (A1+A2)/2 - (B1+B2)/2 within each block; floor_cmp_j = max(max_i|delta_i|, |mean(delta)| + t_{0.975,9} * s_delta * sqrt(1.1)); abba_delta_j reported is mean(delta) across the 10 blocks, spread_j is s_delta. n counts strict-valid bundles (absolute) or strict-valid ABBA blocks (comparative), per the doc's single n definition. n = 10 in every cell, so the 5<=n<10 small-sample guard factor does NOT apply. The output schema has only floor_abs_j, so the two ABBA rows carry floor_cmp_j in that field (labeled in window_class). All values computed from per-bundle summary_metrics.json, cross-checked against campaign_log.jsonl member records, and the mid-gross cell replayed by independent hand arithmetic (exact match).\n\nANOMALIES / CAVEATS: (1) The task said 'per shape cell mid/long' but the campaign executed mid/short: block 08_optional_long_request_absolute has ZERO rows in campaign_log.jsonl — no long-prompt/long-decode request floors exist; short is the second shape actually run, and is what is reported. (2) energy_request_j == idle_subtracted_energy_j exactly (0.0 difference) in all 60 bundles — one idle-subtracted metric under two names; rows are merged accordingly. Gross-vs-idle-sub mid gap (24.0593 - 23.9301 = 0.1293 J) is consistent with idle_mean ~0.119 W times window duration. (3) Claim-readiness anomaly: every one of the 60 bundles has claim_evidence_classification 'flagged', and window_evidence_precheck.gross_request / idle_subtracted_request is eligible=false on ALL 60 — reason clock_bound_exceeds_quarter_window on all (clock_anchor_bound_s ~1.089 s vs 0.25 x window duration ~1.33 s mid / ~0.36 s short), plus cadence_ratio_below_threshold on all 10 short bundles (cadence_ratio ~3.19 < required 4.0). Per §Claim-Gate Thresholds these floors are computable but the underlying request windows currently fail the L2/L3 evidence precheck; P2-037/P2-039 adjudication needed before these floors gate claims. (4) DF-CMP-ABBA-RQ floor_cmp (0.909 J gross) exceeds the absolute floor (0.527 J) — expected per §Comparative Floors; driven by sign-flipping late blocks b07-b10 (deltas +0.457, -0.640, +0.360, -0.535), which look like a drift/ordering pattern in the session tail. (5) All 60 bundles strict_valid=true, status succeeded, collection usable; ABBA block membership complete 4/4 in all 10 blocks. (6) Process note: the codex MCP tool surface was not available in this session (ToolSearch returned no codex tools), so the extraction was done at the lead bench with deterministic scripts instead of a delegated Sol session; every reported number was read directly from bundle artifacts and the headline cell was independently re-derived by hand."

docs/strategy/2026-08-07-paper-portfolio/proposals/prop-mtp-energy.md:3461:docs/site/readme.html:1:<!DOCTYPE html> <html lang="en"> <head> <meta charset="utf-8"> <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> <title>README - JouleWise</title> <script>document.documentElement.classList.add("js-enabled");</script> <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css"> <link rel="icon" href="data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 100 100'><text y='.9em' font-size='90'>⚡</text></svg>"> </head> <body> <header class="site"> <nav class="nav"> <a class="brand" href="index.html"><span class="dot"></span>JOULEWISE</a> <div class="links"> <a href="index.html">Project</a> <a href="research.html">Learn</a> <a href="advisor_brief.html">Advisor Brief</a> <a href="project_status.html">Status</a> <a href="status.html">Live Status</a> <a href="roadmap.html">Roadmap</a> <a href="process.html">Process</a> <a href="record.html">Record</a> <a href="library.html" class="active">Sources</a> <a href="results.html">Measurements</a> </div> </nav> </header> <main> <div class="doc-layout"> <aside class="toc-sidebar"><div class="card-label">Table of contents</div><a href="#current-state">Current State</a> <a href="#verify">Verify</a> <a href="#release">Release</a> <a href="#run-the-harness-mock-target-no-hardware-or-extras-needed">Run The Harness (mock target — no hardware or extras needed)</a> <a href="#config-and-schema-verbs">Config And Schema Verbs</a> <a href="#documentation-map">Documentation Map</a></aside> <div class="doc-wrap doc-source-readme-md"> <p class="doc-meta"><a href="library.html">Back to sources</a> · rendered from <code>README.md</code></p> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="README.md · commit 1af9f92"><span class="source-file">README.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit 1af9f92</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise</h1> <p>JouleWise is an extensible measurement harness for energy-wise LLM inference across heterogeneous local hardware. The benchmark layered on that harness is the frozen workload suite, run rules, and strict validator. The name is a deliberate nod to JouleSort and Splitwise: energy measurement as the spine, split inference as the first major research application.</p> <p>The harness is designed around three stable ideas:</p> <ul> <li>Typed experiment configs define what should run.</li> <li>Runtime and telemetry adapters define how each hardware target is exercised and measured.</li> <li>Run bundles preserve raw traces, events, metadata, logs, and summary metrics for later audit and analysis.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Status:</strong> research prototype. The Mac (Apple M3 Max) measurement harness has completed its instrument repair (D-078 phase 0) and the repaired path has collected 229 strict members across four bracketed windows, a5-a8. Those windows are non-claim-bearing diagnostic, instrument-proving evidence, not published floors. The SCREEN+BUDGET rules are ratified and merged (D-078 clause 10; council C-033): they screen gross and idle-subtracted energy separately, retain a nonzero drift allowance for each family, require a fresh 24-hour bound, reject fallback-clock members from floor cells, and bar mock evidence from claims. The next step is one clean prospective quiet-machine window following <code>docs/phase_2/window_runbook.md</code>, producing the first claim-grade floors before the a8 re-verdict and Splitwise sizing.</p> <p>The post-audit architectural verdicts remain deliberately bounded: AXI-SB is <code>supported</code> for native static-batch runtime feasibility with request-scoped observability, while AXI-SC is <code>unsupported_for_joulewise</code> on the pinned runtime because the required speculative-decode/MTP observability or execution surface is absent. Neither is energy evidence. This summary does not select work: the generated state-kernel regions in <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> and <code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code> own live gates and next-task state. Quiet-machine execution still requires the lead-controlled hardware lane with Ed. The verified end-user quickstart remains a Phase 5 deliverable.</p> <h2 id="current-state">Current State</h2> <p>Phase 1 is in its final stretch; <strong>Phase 2&#39;s Mac vertical slice is complete and the project has its first real energy measurements</strong> (2026-07-06). From a typed config, one command produces a complete, schema-valid, auditable run bundle and reduces it to energy/latency summary metrics — proven first on deterministic mock adapters, and now live on real hardware: the MLX runtime + <code>powermetrics</code> telemetry adapters measured Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (4-bit) on an Apple M3 Max. <strong>P2-003, gross energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~47.2 J per 512-token request. <strong>P2-003, idle-subtracted energy — M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails:</strong> ~44.4 J per request and ~79-90 mJ per generated output token (mean 86.8 mJ). Throughput was 257 tok/s. These are legacy L1 preliminary observations (pre-2M, manual review) under <code>docs/contracts/claims_ladder.md</code>; metric bases per <code>docs/contracts/token_normalization.md</code>. The six real corpus bundles pass <code>validate-bundle --strict</code> read-only and unrewritten: strict re-derives the recorded powermetrics power trace from raw plist evidence, re-derives summary metrics from the recorded trace and event log, checks the legacy additive summary comparison, and requires shape-valid provenance for new-era bundles. This validates the recorded evidence path; it does not independently rerun the hardware session.</p> <p>Unless a figure explicitly states otherwise, JouleWise uses gross measured energy within the named measurement boundary as the headline basis. Gross energy retains the idle, model-residency, and runtime overhead present during the measured interval, so comparisons across devices, configurations, and split versus monolithic execution use gross energy. Idle-subtracted energy is reported separately as a within-device secondary view of activity above the measured idle baseline; it is not used to rank devices or configurations. In Q4, the fixed term is estimated from the gross-energy workload sweep and is not set equal to measured idle energy. The advisor-review rationale and full basis/boundary rule are recorded in <a href="PROJECT_STATUS.md#measurement-methodology-highlights"><code>PROJECT_STATUS.md</code></a>.</p> <p>Under D-070, static batching, speculative decoding / native MTP, MoE versus dense execution, quantization, and reasoning-length variance are five stress tests of Q4&#39;s single thesis. The harness must instrument all five axes and all five have strict-valid L0 smoke-bundle support plus characterization commitments, but every study remains floor-gated, capped at L2, and sequenced after Window A. See the fuller <a href="PROJECT_STATUS.md#summary">Q4 architectural stress-test agenda</a> in <code>PROJECT_STATUS.md</code>.</p> <p>D-075 now folds a ranked extension-axis evaluation into that same agenda without proliferating theses: DSpark/DFlash break-even and control riders, on-device quantized KV, one named hybrid pair, and attached cache/context/kernel/backend provenance work. Every admitted unit remains a floor-gated candidate at or below L2 with a named forbidden upgrade; unresolved runtime and device-fit questions stay NEEDS-WEB, and Ed retains commitment authority. Separate lead-run DSpark/DFlash smokes established native MLX execution and per-round observability only. Their thinking-mode, unmatched-output throughput inversion is hypothesis-generating, not energy evidence.</p> <p>Window A remains open and still requires Ed and a quiet Mac. The repaired instrument has produced the 229-member a5-a8 diagnostic collection, and the merged screening and uncertainty-budget rules (D-078 clause 10) are ready for prospective use. The next claim attempt must follow the run-book: mint the drift bound inside the quiet window, then collect a start triplet, midpoint reference, and end triplet around the science members. A passing window will support the first claim-grade floors; only then do the a8 re-verdict and Splitwise sizing follow. The earlier 222-bundle floor publication remains a caveated historical record. Use the generated state kernel—not this summary—to select the next live or agent-lane step.</p> <p>A separate nine-bundle follow-on is now available as an explicitly <strong>exploratory, unmatched, no-claim</strong> observation block. All nine bundles are strict-valid and collection-usable but claim-evidence-flagged; each model ran three repetitions of the fixed five-item sentinel shape and emitted 1,280 generated output tokens per bundle.</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>unmatched configuration</th> <th align="right">mean gross suite energy — Apple M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails (CPU + GPU + ANE)</th> <th align="right">mean gross energy/generated output token — same boundary</th> <th align="right">runtime-observed output throughput</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>OLMoE-1B-7B BF16</td> <td align="right">229.028 J</td> <td align="right">178.928 mJ/token</td> <td align="right">122.361 tok/s</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Qwen3-4B INT4</td> <td align="right">362.772 J</td> <td align="right">283.416 mJ/token</td> <td align="right">106.519 tok/s</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Qwen3.5-122B-A10B INT4</td> <td align="right">1072.273 J</td> <td align="right">837.713 mJ/token</td> <td align="right">39.473 tok/s</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>These points differ in model scale, architecture, tokenizer, and quantization, so they do not establish a controlled scaling relation, architecture effect, or efficiency comparison. The stored per-generated-token field is idle-subtracted and appears only as D-067&#39;s labeled within-device secondary view in the <a href="docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-exploratory-block/results.md">bundle-cited extraction</a>, which also records spreads, every repetition, the floor comparison, and the Qwen thinking/config caveats.</p> <p>Remaining backends plug into the same adapter interfaces: the fixture-first 2K NVIDIA stack (SSH transport, node worker, nvidia-smi + vLLM adapters) includes NV-GATE-2 software hardening: per-backend raw-lineage verifier registration, usage-first vLLM streaming, and identity-aware process-survival handling. The NV-5 localhost lead gate passed 3/3, but ALL remote protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL pending first live hardware contact; Jetson Orin (2L) remains gated on device access.</p> <p>The landed C-028 arc includes the frozen analysis manifest, the production-uncertainty path, the campaign-verdict split, idle-dependence/HAC uncertainty, the inter-token metric, doctor preflight, and the contrast/claim engine. The analysis trio—manifest, verdict split, and contrast/claim engine—is complete. The six frozen legacy arms and 0.3.x/0.4.x dispatch rules remain explicit; landed software is not being presented as new live evidence. P0-003 closed with an iCloud Drive backup and a fresh restore that was strict-valid and byte-identical. No new live NVIDIA or quiet-Mac measurement is claimed here.</p> <p>The post-audit landings add request-scoped AXI-SA burst/decode semantics, freeze SPLIT-AP Part I before outcomes, close SITE-02&#39;s discovery and emitted-code regression work, and establish AXI-SB&#39;s <code>supported</code> verdict from lead-run B=2/B=4 Metal probes. The probes establish runtime feasibility and request observability only; they add no energy result. The corresponding AXI-SC pinned-runtime spike returned <code>unsupported_for_joulewise</code>: the external- draft path lacks the full proposal/acceptance/decode-boundary observability contract, and native MTP lacks a usable generation surface. No Mac energy leg was minted from that negative applicability result.</p> <p>The repository currently contains:</p> <ul> <li>Typed config and output schemas with JSON-Schema export and validation.</li> <li>Runtime, telemetry, and transport interface contracts, with shipped mock adapters and a backend registry.</li> <li>The runnable harness: bundle writer, controller lifecycle, reducer, a shared bundle read layer, static HTML report generator, and a CLI (<code>run</code>, <code>validate-bundle</code>, <code>reduce</code>, <code>report</code>).</li> <li>Example Mac-local and mock-local configs.</li> <li>Phase 1 methodology, feasibility, and measurement-design docs.</li> <li>A test suite run in CI on every push, including a mock end-to-end run and bundle validation. The canonical command below and CI output own the current result; reader docs intentionally do not copy its volatile count.</li> </ul> <h2 id="verify">Verify</h2> <pre><code class="language-bash">python3 -m unittest discover -s tests

<!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. <h1>JouleWise: Project Status, Plan, And Architecture</h1> <p>Audience: project advisor. This is the standalone monitoring document - it summarizes what the project is, how it is built, where it stands, and what it needs, without requiring any other file. Pointers into the repository are provided for anyone who wants the full evidence trail.</p> <ul> <li>Freshness owner: phase completion lives in the phase exit checklists; live gates and work selection live only in the generated state-kernel regions of <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> and <code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code>; the canonical suite command and CI own the current verification result. This page deliberately does not duplicate volatile commit, pull-request, queue, or test-count facts.</li> <li>Repository state: <code>main</code> contains the repaired measurement instrument (D-078 phase 0) and the audited screening and uncertainty-budget rules (D-078 clause 10; council C-033). The repaired-instrument collection has 229 members across four bracketed windows, a5-a8. Those windows are useful diagnostic evidence that the instrument works, but they are not claim-bearing and do not yet publish a floor. The next step is one clean prospective quiet-machine collection following <code>docs/phase_2/window_runbook.md</code>; if it passes, it will produce the first claim-grade floors before the a8 re-verdict and Splitwise sizing.</li> <li>Project phase: see the phase exit checklists for exact completion state; live eligibility and next work come from the generated state kernel, not this reader-facing summary.</li> <li>Repository: <code>github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</code> (branch <code>main</code>)</li> <li>Live status site: <a href="https://quiet-signal-6af8833395.lakebed.app">https://quiet-signal-6af8833395.lakebed.app</a> (Lakebed capsule; it is an Ed-deployed snapshot, not the repository authority. <code>docs/site/DRIFT.md</code> records known differences; agents refresh that report when front-facing state changes and never regenerate or deploy the site.)</li> </ul> <h2 id="current-repository-view-30-second-read">Current Repository View — 30-second read</h2> <p><strong>The repaired instrument has completed its first collection era, but the first claim-grade floor is still ahead.</strong> The D-078 phase-0 repair fixed the timing and calibration path on 2026-07-22. Four bracketed windows then collected 229 strict members (a5-a8). They are retained as non-claim-bearing diagnostic, instrument-proving evidence: they showed that the repaired path works and exposed the remaining drift-screen problem, but they are not a published floor set.</p> <p>That problem is now resolved in the merged SCREEN+BUDGET rules (D-078 clause 10). Gross and idle-subtracted energy are screened separately; each passing window keeps a nonzero drift allowance in its uncertainty budget; the drift bound expires after 24 hours; fallback-clock members cannot support a floor; and mock evidence is identified from the bound configuration and barred from claims. The next quiet session will mint its bound inside the window and collect three start references, one midpoint reference, and three end references. The older 222-bundle floor table below remains visible as a caveated historical record, not the current measurement posture.</p> <p>AXI-SB remains <code>supported</code> for native static-batch runtime feasibility with request-scoped observability; AXI-SC is <code>unsupported_for_joulewise</code> on the pinned runtime because the required speculative-decode/MTP observability or execution surface is absent. Neither verdict is an energy result. Remote protocol pins remain PROVISIONAL, and the generated state kernel remains the work-selection authority.</p> <h3>Published Window-A floor summary</h3> <blockquote> <p><strong>CAVEAT (2026-07-19 soundness audit):</strong> a trace-time-anchor defect was found in the powermetrics evidence path (power timestamps misaligned with runtime events at the ~0.5–1 s scale). Its gross request energy moved by 7.659 J; the idle-subtracted within-device secondary view moved by 6.608 J (same boundary). Verified extraction: <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-floor-extraction/extraction-verified.json</code>; reader deliverable: <code>docs/advisor_briefs/2026-07-17-window-a-brief.html</code>.</p> <h3>2026-07-19 re-calibration under the environment guard — PRELIMINARY</h3> <p>The caveated suite rows were re-measured in two bracketed windows under the D-077 guard: <strong>94 strict-valid bundles</strong>, all admission predicates satisfied. Reviewed readout: suite gross <strong>147.96 ± 0.39 J</strong> clean (contaminated cells were ~+30%); frozen-estimator provisional comparative floor <strong>≈ 1.13 J (~0.77%)</strong> from 5 of 10 planned ABBA blocks (~22× tighter, same estimator, than the caveated figure); long-decode <strong>83.9 mJ/output-token</strong>, matching the 07-17 decode cell to ~0.1%. That corpus was claim-ineligible on source provenance (dirty collection tree); details: <code>docs/advisor_briefs/2026-07-19-recalibration-update.html</code>.</p> <p>UPDATE (2026-07-19 night): the clean re-run is done — 288 strict-valid bundles with clean source provenance (<code>runs_recal3/4/5/6_20260719/</code>) cover every planned Window-A cell except DF-TELEM at planned n, including the complete n=10 suite-ABBA comparative cell; the source provenance gate is closed. <strong>SUPERSEDING UPDATE (2026-07-19/20): a same-day soundness audit found a timing bug, and no energy number from the existing recordings will be used for claims until re-measurement.</strong> In plain terms: the power meter and the workload log time on two different clocks, and our alignment between them could be off by up to ~1 second. Energy is computed by summing meter samples inside the workload&#39;s start/stop window, so a misaligned window integrates the wrong slice of the recording — dramatic for sub-second test runs (one 0.37 s run read 0.27 J when its true consumption, plainly present in the recording, was <del>8 J), and a meaningful hidden uncertainty (</del>±10 J) even on 60-second runs. Nothing measured negative; the recordings are intact and self-consistent; long-run repeatability (~0.3% across nights) shows the platform is stable. Very short workloads are simply below this instrument&#39;s resolution and will not be claimed — by design, not workaround. The fix (align on the meter&#39;s own timestamps, attach an explicit uncertainty range to every number, calibrate end-to-end with 40 precisely-timed GPU bursts before new data) is implemented and in adversarial review. Plain-language explainer: <code>docs/advisor_briefs/2026-07-20-timing-defect-explainer.md</code>; technical record: <code>docs/reviews/2026-07-19-measurement-soundness-audit.md</code>.</p> <p><strong>REPAIR COMPLETE (2026-07-22): the instrument repair is finished and signed off.</strong> Over three days the timing defect was fixed and the whole measurement chain was hardened through nine rounds of independent adversarial review (each round tried to break the instrument; the last round found one remaining gap, recorded below). In plain terms, the instrument now: (a) knows precisely when its power readings happened relative to the model&#39;s work (the clock-alignment fix, with the alignment uncertainty — about 27 milliseconds — carried into every result as an explicit error bar); (b) proves its own calibration is genuine and fresh — a calibration recording that was tampered with, mislabeled, taken under the wrong procedure, or older than 24 hours is automatically rejected; and (c) refuses to report a result rather than report a doubtful one, in every failure case we could construct. One known limitation is recorded honestly: the file that stores the detection-floor statistics is not yet cryptographically tied back to the raw measurements it came from, so we only trust such files when our own pipeline produced them in the same verified session (a fix is queued). Live validation on the real hardware passed: the validation recording (made under the earlier 40-pulse calibration procedure) detected all 40 calibration pulses with no false detections, and a test measurement reproduced the expected physics where the old defective pipeline had been wrong by a factor of ~28. Production measurements will use the newer 59-pulse calibration procedure, which supports the stronger statistical guarantee we quote for the timing error bar. Next: a fresh calibration and re-collection of the measurement campaign under the repaired instrument. Record: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-20-p0-instrument-repair.md</code>.</p> <p><strong>COLLECTION ERA UPDATE (2026-07-24): the repaired instrument has now been proven in production.</strong> Over two nights we collected 229 clean measurements across four properly-bracketed windows. The standout result: two identical reference measurements taken three hours apart agreed to within 0.007 joules on a ~38.5 joule task — about 0.02%, which is excellent repeatability for whole-system power measurement. The windows are not yet &quot;claim-grade&quot; for one honest reason: our own stability check (comparing a reference task at each window&#39;s start and end) was found to be asking a mathematically unanswerable question, so it failed every window on a technicality while the underlying data was good. After a formal debate between the two AI models working on the project — which the reviewing model won on one substantive point — the check was redesigned and ratified: windows are now screened for anomalous drift against a limit derived from measured repeatability (instead of an arbitrary constant), and any drift observed is carried into the results&#39; error bars rather than being ignored once a window &quot;passes&quot;. Reference measurements are also being tripled at each window edge. One collection session under the new rules produces the project&#39;s first claim-grade detection-floor table, which then sizes the Splitwise replication experiments. Records: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-23-window-a-collection-arc.md</code>, decision log D-078 clauses 8-10.</p> <p><strong>SCREENING RULES BUILT, AUDITED, AND MERGED (2026-07-25; council C-033).</strong> The redesigned stability screen described above is now implemented and on main: both energy families are screened separately, every passing window carries an explicit drift allowance into its error bars, drift limits expire after 24 hours so stale calibrations cannot be reused, and a measurement whose internal clock had to be guessed can never anchor a result (that one rule alone corrected a floor that was overstated by roughly a factor of three). The code went through an unusually deep adversarial review — four independent audit rounds and three rounds of cross-examination between two different AI models — which caught and fixed several ways the new rules could have been silently bypassed. The step-by-step measurement procedure for the next collection session is written up in <code>docs/phase_2/window_runbook.md</code>. Records: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-24-screen-budget-gauntlet.md</code>, council log C-033.</p> <h3>Exploratory follow-on — not a promoted claim</h3> <p>Nine additional strict-valid, collection-usable bundles cover three repetitions each of unmatched OLMoE-1B-7B BF16, Qwen3-4B INT4, and Qwen3.5-122B-A10B INT4 configurations on the fixed five-item <code>jw_mixed_v1_sentinel</code> shape. Every bundle is claim-evidence-flagged, the model/config points differ in architecture, scale, tokenizer, and quantization, and the repetition count is below the headline protocol. The values are therefore descriptive <strong>EXPLORATORY / L1-legacy observations only</strong>.</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>unmatched configuration</th> <th align="right">mean gross suite energy — Apple M3 Max / powermetrics SoC rails (CPU + GPU + ANE)</th> <th align="right">mean gross energy/generated output token — same boundary</th> <th align="right">runtime-observed output throughput</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>OLMoE-1B-7B BF16</td> <td align="right">229.028 J (227.141–231.790 J)</td> <td align="right">178.928 mJ/token (177.454–181.086 mJ/token)</td> <td align="right">122.361 tok/s (122.261–122.481 tok/s)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Qwen3-4B INT4</td> <td align="right">362.772 J (362.642–362.903 J)</td> <td align="right">283.416 mJ/token (283.314–283.518 mJ/token)</td> <td align="right">106.519 tok/s (106.470–106.545 tok/s)</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Qwen3.5-122B-A10B INT4</td> <td align="right">1072.273 J (1061.722–1085.144 J)</td> <td align="right">837.713 mJ/token (829.471–847.769 mJ/token)</td> <td align="right">39.473 tok/s (39.349–39.569 tok/s)</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Each bundle emitted 1,280 generated output tokens.
